questions.stem: In India, which sector contributes the LARGEST share of GDP currently?
questions.explanation: Services sector contributes >50% of India's GDP. Industry ~26%, Agriculture ~15%. But agriculture still EMPLOYS ~44% of the workforce — the classic 'structural mismatch' of India's economy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is classified as a PRIMARY sector activity?
questions.explanation: Primary = extraction from nature: agriculture, fishing, forestry, mining. Secondary = manufacturing / industry (cement, cars, steel). Tertiary = services (banking, IT, trade, transport). Quaternary = knowledge-intensive (R&D). Quinary = high-level decision-making (policy, CEO).

questions.stem: Under MGNREGA (2005), each rural household is guaranteed at least ___ days of wage employment a year:
questions.explanation: MGNREGA — Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (2005), effective 2006. Guarantees 100 days of unskilled wage labour per rural household per year, within 5 km of the home or travel allowance. Now extended to 150 days in some drought-hit districts.

questions.stem: Match the INDUSTRY with its KEY INDIAN LOCATION. A. Jute.  B. Cotton textiles.  C. Iron & steel.  D. IT / software. List-II: 1. Kolkata belt (WB).  2. Mumbai-Ahmedabad.  3. Jamshedpur (Jharkhand).  4. Bengaluru / Hyderabad.
questions.explanation: Jute — West Bengal (Hooghly belt; India is world's largest jute producer). Cotton — Mumbai 'Cottonopolis', Ahmedabad ('Manchester of India'). Iron & steel — TISCO (1907) at Jamshedpur. IT — Bengaluru 'Silicon Valley of India', Hyderabad 'Cyberabad'.

Stock market indicators tied to the colour blue

questions.explanation: Blue economy — sustainable use of ocean resources: fisheries, shipping, offshore oil/gas, coastal tourism, marine renewable energy. India launched 'Draft Blue Economy Policy' framework in 2021. Green economy = sustainability focus on land/forest.

questions.stem: Consider the following about NITI AAYOG. 1. It replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015. 2. Its full name is 'National Institution for Transforming India'. 3. The Prime Minister is its Chairperson ex officio. 4. Unlike the Planning Commission, it does NOT allocate funds to states. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. NITI Aayog is a policy think-tank, not a statutory or constitutional body. Vice-Chairperson (full-time executive head) currently: Suman Bery (2022 onwards). Fund allocation to states moved to the Finance Ministry.

questions.stem: The 'INFORMAL' / 'UNORGANISED' sector in India broadly employs what fraction of the workforce?
questions.explanation: Informal sector (small enterprises, self-employed, contract workers, farm labour) employs roughly 80-90% of India's workforce but contributes ~50% of GDP — the classic informality trap. Formalisation efforts include GST registration, Udyam portal (MSMEs), e-Shram (unorganised workers).
